page: Amazon Web Services c8in.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors. The instance provides 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, supported by 384.0 GB of system memory. Operating at a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the hardware configuration focuses resource density heavily on raw processing throughput.

The server features high network throughput with a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps, suited for communication-heavy distributed architectures. It does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring persistence to be managed via remote or attached network storage such as EBS. No discrete graphical processing units are included in this profile, directing all computational tasks entirely to the Intel CPU cores.

Because of the dedicated bare-metal architecture and 300 Gbps networking capabilities, the c8in.metal-48xl provides substantial compute density without hypervisor overhead. The configuration fits high-performance computing, large-scale distributed simulations, network appliance virtualization, continuous integration clusters, and compute-heavy batch processing pipelines that rely on massive CPU throughput and extreme network performance.
description: Amazon Web Services c8in.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture with Intel processors. It features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The instance features a 300 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for high-throughput node communications. It includes no integrated local storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage solutions for stateful data persistence. The absence of hypervisor overhead combined with dedicated high-frequency cores makes it suitable for intensive parallel processing. Common deployments include high-performance computing workloads, large batch processing pipelines, network function virtualization, and distributed compute clusters requiring maximum CPU and network throughput.
